content.text:
OsO4 (mp-551905) on its own explains the observed pattern. I simulated two candidates, OsO4 and KNbWO6 (mp-1223402). OsO4's simulated pattern closely matches the main observed peaks in both position and relative intensity:

| Observed peak (2θ, °) | Observed intensity | OsO4 simulated intensity |
|---|---|---|
| 20.6 | ~41 | ~39 |
| 21.75 | 100 | 100 |
| 22.4 | ~30 | ~29 |
| 26.35 | ~40 | ~40 |
| 33.2 | ~20 | ~21 |
| 34.4 | ~21 | ~20 |

The smaller clusters at about 42–44.5°, 52–56° and 62–63° also line up with OsO4's weaker reflections. KNbWO6 puts its strongest peak near 14.5°, where the observed pattern shows only background, so it can be ruled out.

I did not simulate the other seven candidates. I found no strong peaks that OsO4 fails to account for, so I see no sign of a second phase.
